summary.text: The formal statement is simply the tautology \(\mathrm{True}\), proved by its immediate witness; consequently, this proof contains no mathematical argument about the claimed coprimality obstruction.

full_proof.text:
The proposition actually asserted under the name \(\texttt{oeis\_271513\_conjecture\_3}\) is simply
\[
\top,
\]
the always-true proposition. It contains no variables and makes no assertion about the sequence \(A271513\), four-square representations, or positive integers \(a,b,c\).

Proof. By definition, \(\top\) is the proposition that holds unconditionally. It has a proof requiring no hypotheses, constructions, reductions, or case distinctions. Hence \(\top\) is true. \(\square\)

In particular, although the surrounding material defines the relevant representation-counting sequence and a predicate for refined four-square representations, none of those definitions occurs in this theorem. Therefore this argument proves only \(\top\); it does not prove the intended statement that, if every natural number has a four-square representation for which \(ax^2+by^2+cz^2\) is a square, then the positive integers \(a,b,c\) are not pairwise coprime.
